Exit: An ancient standing stone etched with glowing runes. Use it to open a gateway to other worlds.
A kit containing everything needed to raise a Portal Hub. Place it anywhere — then use the portal to travel to other worlds.
You begin with a Portal Kit. Place it anywhere to open a gateway to other worlds.
Bind a witch stone into fresh fur and dried wolfsbane, sealed with animal fat. Assembles a portable Portal Hub kit.

A small metal nail, perfect for joining wood. It is the metal it was made from: copper, ghost bronze, tin, tin bronze, white bronze or iron. Heat it and strike it with a hard hammer to raise its quality; each nail takes only a few strikes.
Hammer a nugget of copper, tin, bronze or iron into a nail of the same metal.

Crafted: From a copper, tin, bronze or iron nugget using a hammer, or six at a time by casting a heated copper, tin or bronze bar (one mud brick and one clay as the mould). The nail is the metal of its nugget or bar. Heat and smith: In a fire or forge it heats up (shown as a Heated nail) and cools again outside it. A heated nail struck with a hard hammer gains quality from your Smithing skill; each nail takes only a few strikes. Uses: Construction and crafting. A nail of any metal works the same in every recipe, iron included. Smelts: Returns 1 nugget of its own metal in a furnace at 1100°C or hotter.

A flat metal sheet, hammered thin. It is the metal it was made from: copper, ghost bronze, tin, tin bronze, white bronze or iron. Heat it and strike it with a hard hammer to raise its quality; each sheet takes only a few strikes.
Hammer a heated bar of copper, ghost bronze, tin, tin bronze or white bronze flat with a hard hammer into a sheet of the same metal. Your Smithing skill adds to its quality.
A tin solder stick for joining metal parts or sealing seams. A new stick lasts five recipes.
Forge 4 iron nuggets into 4 Iron Nails (Metal Nails of Metal Type 200).
Melt a tin-grade metal nugget into a solder stick that lasts five recipes.
Hammer 6 iron nuggets flat into an Iron Sheet (a Metal Sheet of Metal Type 200), ready for iron-grade tools and armor.
Hammer a heated Ghost Bronze, Tin, Tin Bronze or White Bronze bar flat with a hard hammer into a sheet of the same metal, ready for alloy armor. Your Smithing skill adds to its quality.
Cast a heated copper, tin or bronze bar into six nails of the same metal.

A refined oil used for oil lamps.
It's also fine to use it for frying food or as a seasoning.
Operation steps: 1. Need to heat fat liquid. 2. Heat and melt 12 pieces of fat in a bowl to obtain a bowl of liquid fat.

A cake of stearin. Can be used as wax for making candles.
It can be thrown directly into a fire, and it is also a very good waterproofing agent and lubricant.
Strike the heated sheet with a hard hammer to raise its quality. Each strike uses one of its strikes.
Strike the heated nail with a hard hammer to raise its quality. Each strike uses one of its strikes.
Pour a small crucible of molten copper, tin or bronze into a mould of mud bricks and clay to cast one sheet of the same metal. Your Smithing skill adds to its quality.

Salt dissolved in water, for pickling and salting food. Food soaking in it is salted, and raw meat or lean fish left in a clay bowl of it cures into Salt-Cured Meat or Fish. A Pickle Vat ferments food in it. Add more salt to make Concentrated Brine.
Very salty. Food left in it is salted.
Dissolve the salt in the water to make Brine.
Dissolve more salt in the brine. Salty enough, it becomes Concentrated Brine.
Raw meat cured in brine. A filling, slow-spoiling travel ration - though the salt will leave you thirsty.
The salt-cured meat has finally spoiled.
Eat the salt-cured meat. Filling, but salty.
Lean fish cured in brine. A light, slow-spoiling travel ration that keeps far longer than dried fish - though the salt will leave you thirsty.
The salt-cured fish has finally spoiled.
Eat the salt-cured fish. Light, but salty.

Raw meat soaking in brine. About two days in the brine turn it into Salt-Cured Meat. Kept in a clay bowl holding at least 100 brine it cures; out of the brine it stops curing and spoils like raw meat. Rinse it to get the raw meat back.
Take it out of the brine. It is raw again and stops curing; it keeps the salt it soaked up.

Raw lean fish soaking in brine. About two days in the brine turn it into Salt-Cured Fish. Kept in a clay bowl holding at least 100 brine it cures; out of the brine it stops curing and spoils like raw fish. Rinse it to get the raw fish back.
Take it out of the brine. It is raw again and stops curing; it keeps the salt it soaked up.
